leads.name: github.com/pelletier/go-toml
leads.note: v1 module; separate implementation from v2.
leads.evidence: toml.LoadBytes on controls/toml/service-config.toml returns the expected typed tree (walked with Tree.Keys/GetPath). On controls/toml/typed-scalars.toml it fails with '(29, 24): parsing error: incorrect date/time separation character: \n' at 'local_date = 1979-05-27'. The v1.9.5 lexer (lexer.go:355, sha256 c46ba00c34d6a706a54b915779c236629252a7e802e5b2a89ae2cf50f4b57013) accepts only EOF, ' ' or 'T' after a local date, so a local date followed by a newline is rejected; the one-line document 'd = 1979-05-27\n' fails at (1, 15) the same way.

leads.name: github.com/naoina/toml
leads.evidence: v0.1.1 (latest tagged release, 2017) implements the TOML 0.4 PEG grammar. toml.Parse accepts controls/toml/service-config.toml but rejects controls/toml/typed-scalars.toml with 'line 7: invalid TOML syntax' at 'octal = 0o755' (TOML 0.5 octal integer); its ast.Datetime.Time() also has no local date, local time or local date-time form.

leads.name: github.com/influxdata/toml
leads.note: Fork of naoina/toml; the only proxy version is the pseudo-version v0.0.0-20180607005434-2a2e3012f7cf (2018-06-07), before TOML 0.5 added local dates. Not run; naoina/toml v0.1.1 failed the second control.
leads.evidence: toml.Unmarshal into map[string]any rejects controls/toml/service-config.toml with 'toml: unmarshal: line 6: `map[string]interface {}.owner' must be struct or map, but interface given' and controls/toml/typed-scalars.toml with 'toml: line 7: parse error' at `octal = 0o755` (TOML 0.4 grammar inherited from naoina/toml). It shares 1,032 of its 1,988 distinct non-test source lines with naoina/toml v0.1.1.
leads.run: Go 1.27.1 (darwin/arm64 host triage module, go get @latest on 2026-11-17)

leads.name: github.com/creachadair/tomledit/parser
leads.note: Syntax-preserving editor; parser package exposes items.
leads.evidence: parser.New(r).Items() accepts both controls but returns each value as a parser.Token holding its token type and raw source text (for example Token{Type: Integer, text: "0xDEAD_BEEF"}, Token{Type: String, text: "\"tab\\tquote...\\u00e9\""}). The package documents that it does not convert values into Go data; a typed tree would require the harness to decode integers, escapes and date-times from the raw text itself, which the protocol excludes.
leads.run: Go 1.27.1 (darwin/arm64 host triage module, go get @latest on 2026-11-17)

leads.name: github.com/midbel/toml
leads.evidence: toml.Decode into map[string]any matches service-config except that it cannot mark kinds: offset, local date-time, local date and local time all come back as time.Time (local kinds in UTC, the offset one in a fixed zone), so a local date-time is indistinguishable from a UTC offset date-time. On typed-scalars the basic-string escape \u00e9 decodes to "I" instead of "é" (observed strings.escapes "tab\tquote\"backslash\\ I").
leads.run: Go 1.27.1 (darwin/arm64 host triage module, go get @latest on 2026-11-17)

leads.name: github.com/komkom/toml
leads.evidence: toml.New(r) is an io.Reader that streams the document as JSON. Both controls convert, but date-times become JSON strings ("1979-05-27T00:32:00.5-07:00", "1979-05-27", "00:32:00.25"), indistinguishable from TOML strings, and numbers are copied as JSON number text (1e3), so the typed tree would need the harness to re-parse the JSON lexemes; the four date-time kinds are lost.
leads.run: Go 1.27.1 (darwin/arm64 host triage module, go get @latest on 2026-11-17)

leads.name: github.com/achun/tom-toml
leads.note: Module v0.2.0 (TOML 0.2-era own parser, 2014-2015) requires no TOML library; likely fails the TOML 1.0 controls. Not run in this round.
leads.evidence: Run on the host against v0.2.0 (README: supports TOML v0.2.0): toml.Parse rejects both controls with "roles does not match one of stageValues" (inline tables and later syntax are not in TOML 0.2.0).

leads.name: github.com/lixenwraith/toml
leads.note: README describes a deterministic TOML subset encoder, decoder and formatter.
leads.evidence: toml.Unmarshal rejects service-config with 'expected newline at line 8' (`since = 1979-05-27T07:32:00Z`) and typed-scalars with 'expected newline at line 5' (`underscored = 1_000_000`): the subset has no date-time values or underscored integers.
leads.run: Go 1.27.1 (darwin/arm64 host triage module, go get @latest on 2026-11-17)

leads.name: github.com/laurent22/toml-go
leads.evidence: A 2014 parser listed on the toml-lang wiki Old page; its Document/Value accessors expose a single GetDate/AsDate time.Time type, so the four TOML 1.0 date-time kinds cannot be told apart. Not run.
leads.found_by: round-4 GitHub repository search (toml parser language:go) and pkg.go.dev queries

leads.name: github.com/kezhuw/toml
leads.note: README: compatible with TOML v0.4.0 (no hexadecimal/octal/binary integers or local date-time kinds), last commit 2019.

leads.name: github.com/tabnas/toml/go
leads.note: Module github.com/tabnas/toml/go v0.5.22 requires no TOML library, so it may be an own parser; Imported-by 2. Not run in this round.
leads.family: tabnas/toml (Go port of the @tabnas/toml Jsonic grammar plugin, on tabnas/parser and tabnas/jsonic)
leads.evidence: Run on the host (go 1.27.1) against v0.5.22: both controls parse, but the README states and the run confirms that every number, integers included, comes back as float64 (integers.hex 3.735928559e+09, floats.exponent 1000), so the typed-scalars control cannot tell the integer kind from the float kind. Date-times are *TomlTime with a kind tag and the original source text. Fails the typed tree.

search_recheck.scope: every hit of the recorded pkg.go.dev snapshot with a positive Imported-by count that was not yet a selected path, lead or exclusion (118 rows, 100 unique packages)
search_recheck.method: go.mod of the module's latest version from proxy.golang.org, searched for requirements on BurntSushi/toml, pelletier/go-toml, naoina/toml, influxdata/toml, go-rotini/toml, creachadair/tomledit, komkom/toml or midbel/toml
search_recheck.finding: Packages that require a TOML library are configuration loaders or wrappers over an already examined parser and are not separate paths. Among the rest, most modules named */toml with v0.3.x/v0.4.x tags (go-forks, patrickhaller, lxlxw, reusee, zannen, jonsen, cxzgb123, cloudradar-monitoring, ando-masaki, FireworkMC, Oneledger, morgulbrut, timob, gozelle, arkdep, go-xe2/third, kcl-go 3rdparty) carry BurntSushi/toml-era version numbers and are forks or vendored copies of BurntSushi/toml or of go-toml v1 (kjzz, winstonprivacyinc, yesnault, gopkg.in/pelletier/go-toml.v1), each with Imported-by 1-6; others are not TOML parsers (go-output, varfmt, tinybind configbind, go-loose-json-parser, Psiphon configloader, Shopify ecfg, stvp/go-toml-config flag loader, vuvuzela encoding). These were classified from module metadata only and were not run.
